root_cause: Only the global 60 s watchdog fails: there are no trace mismatches, no compile errors, and no failing suites, so the core never reaches the ECALL retirement/halt point or never completes an outstanding request. This is a liveness/handshake deadlock rather than wrong data. Because the previously patched commit/DCache/ALU/ID/IF/PRF/ROB/top files are falsified, the remaining liveness-critical logic is concentrated in the untouched I-cache refill/response path and the issue/rename/LSU accept-ready queues: an in-flight fetch or memory request is most likely retracted or its response dropped, or an allocation queue stops re-asserting ready/valid, freezing forward progress.
repair_constraints: Never rename ports, modules, or file paths; preserve every interface in the plan contract exactly.
Keep reset synchronous and active-low: it takes effect only on a clk rising edge, and dmem_valid must be 0 during reset.

Preserve external handshake rules: at most one outstanding request per interface; once valid/addr are asserted they must remain stable until ready; do not abort or retract an in-flight request on flush or halt; halt/flush may only suppress the response via epoch gating.
During normal execution imem_addr[1:0] must remain 00; the TB may insert deterministic and changing wait cycles, so ready must not be assumed high.

Preserve ECALL/halt timing: ECALL stays valid through ID/EX/MEM/WB; exactly one dbg_retire_valid is produced at the commit edge; halted=1 and exit_code=x10 appear on the next clk edge; no cycle may have halted=0 with exit_code!=0, and all outputs/architectural state stay stable after halt.
Preserve retirement semantics: exactly one single-cycle dbg_retire_valid per truly committed instruction, at most one per cycle; stalls/flushes must not duplicate or lose retire events.
Any queue fix must use consistent FIFO head/tail/count bookkeeping, must not overwrite an unconsumed entry, and must drive every module output from real internal state.
Do not regress the previously verified baseline behavior in modules outside this patch; if touching them, restore rather than redefine interface behavior.
